title: Java User Input
learningObjectives: Create a Scanner to read console input.
Read text and numeric values with the correct Scanner methods.
Understand token-based input and line-based input.
Validate simple input before using it.
Close input resources when the program owns them.

understand.concept: Java programs can receive information while they run. The Scanner class in java.util reads tokens and lines from an input source such as System.in. Choose nextInt or nextDouble for numeric tokens and nextLine for a complete line. Be aware that nextLine consumes the remainder of the current line, which matters after numeric reads. Real applications should validate input and handle invalid values rather than assuming every response is correct.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic helps Java developers select and use the right standard-library tools for java user input in maintainable applications.
understand.analogy: Think of the collection or date API as a purpose-built tool: its operations communicate the guarantees your program can rely on.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a guide; Java API contracts, equality rules and exception behaviour determine the actual result.

explain.narrative: Import java.util.Scanner, create a Scanner for System.in, read values, and use them in calculations or decisions. Scanner separates tokens by whitespace by default. next() reads one token; nextLine() reads the rest of a line. After nextInt(), a following nextLine() may first return the leftover newline. Consume that newline when you need the next full line. For robust programs, check hasNextInt before reading or handle InputMismatchException. Close a Scanner that owns a resource; closing a Scanner around System.in also closes System.in, so avoid closing it early when a larger application still needs console input.

examples.title: Read a name
examples.code:
import java.util.Scanner;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner in = new Scanner("Asha"); String name = in.next(); System.out.println("Hello, " + name); } }
examples.explanation: next reads one whitespace-delimited token from the supplied input stream.

examples.title: Read an integer
examples.code:
import java.util.Scanner;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner in = new Scanner("18"); int age = in.nextInt(); System.out.println(age + 1); } }
examples.explanation: nextInt parses the next token as an int.

examples.title: Read a decimal
examples.code:
import java.util.Scanner;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner in = new Scanner("12.5"); double price = in.nextDouble(); System.out.printf("%.2f%n", price * 2); } }
examples.explanation: nextDouble reads a decimal numeric token.

examples.title: Read a full line
examples.code:
import java.util.Scanner;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner in = new Scanner("Java collections are useful"); String line = in.nextLine(); System.out.println(line.toUpperCase()); } }
examples.explanation: nextLine preserves spaces within the line.

examples.title: Check numeric input
examples.code:
import java.util.Scanner;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner in = new Scanner("42 words"); if (in.hasNextInt()) System.out.println(in.nextInt()); else System.out.println("Not an integer"); System.out.println(in.next()); } }
examples.explanation: hasNextInt checks the next token before parsing it.

practise.guidedTask: Create a small Java program demonstrating java user input. Predict each result, then compile and run it with JDK 21.
practise.independentTask: Build an original practical program using java user input. Include at least two test cases, expected outputs, and a short explanation of your API choices and edge cases.
hints: Scanner.nextInt reads a token, while nextLine reads the remainder of the current line; account for the leftover newline when mixing them.
Validate user input before using it, and handle InputMismatchException or malformed values deliberately.
Test valid input, invalid tokens, empty lines and end-of-input so the console loop cannot become stuck.
practise.challenge: Extend one java user input example to handle a realistic edge case and explain the behaviour using the Java API contract.

questions.prompt: Which class is commonly used to read console input?
questions.explanation: Scanner in java.util reads tokens and lines from input sources.

questions.prompt: Which method reads a complete remaining line?
questions.explanation: nextLine returns the rest of the current line, including spaces.
nextInt parses the next token as an integer.

questions.prompt: Why can nextLine appear to return an empty string after nextInt?
questions.answer: The newline remains in the input
options: The newline remains in the input
questions.explanation: The line break after the numeric token is still waiting to be consumed.

questions.answer: Checking whether the next token can be read as an int
options: Checking whether the next token can be read as an int
questions.explanation: It allows a program to test the next token before parsing.
